problem: End-to-End Autonomous Driving systems suffer from manual sequential ordering (perception-prediction-planning) causing information loss and cumulative errors, plus inefficiency in handling spatiotemporal input.
approach: DriveMamba integrates dynamic task relation modeling and implicit view correspondence learning into a single-stage Unified Mamba decoder using sparse token representations sorted by 3D spatial positions.
contribution: DriveMamba demonstrates superior performance on nuScenes and Bench2Drive datasets, achieving efficient long-context token modeling for end-to-end autonomous driving.

problem: Image editing and in-context generation struggle to ensure physical consistency where edited objects remain coherent, especially critical for world simulation tasks.
approach: ChronoEdit reframes image editing as video generation, treating input and edited images as first and last frames, then performs temporal reasoning at inference time with explicit physics constraints.
contribution: ChronoEdit surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in both visual fidelity and physical plausibility on the new PBench-Edit benchmark.

problem: Joint multimodal learning often overfits certain modalities while neglecting others, leading to performance inferior to unimodal learning due to modality competition.
approach: TCMax maximizes total correlation between multimodal features and labels using Total Correlation Neural Estimation (TCNE), a hyperparameter-free loss based on information-theoretic principles.
contribution: TCMax outperforms state-of-the-art joint and unimodal learning approaches by alleviating modality competition while capturing inter-modal interactions.

problem: Model merging research lacks a benchmark for Multimodal LLMs, and merging different modalities into a unified model remains unexplored.
approach: OptMerge introduces a model merging benchmark for MLLMs with 10 implemented algorithms, proposing a novel method that removes noise from task vectors and robustly optimizes merged vectors.
contribution: The proposed method achieves an average performance gain of 2.48% and demonstrates that model merging enables building improved MLLMs without training data.

problem: Multimodal dataset distillation fails to capture complex dynamically evolving knowledge embedded in later training stages of teacher models, causing degraded student performance.
approach: PTM-ST uses stage-aware teacher modeling and shortcut-based trajectory construction to accurately fit the teacher's learning dynamics across distinct training phases.
contribution: PTM-ST achieves up to 13.5% absolute improvement and an average gain of 9.53% on Flickr30k while reducing storage overhead.

problem: Tool-augmented LLM policies trained as single monolithic systems scale poorly with long horizons and diverse tools, and generalize weakly to new scenarios.
approach: AgentFlow decomposes work across four specialized modules (planner, executor, verifier, generator) and trains on-policy via Flow-based Group Refined Policy Optimization (Flow-GRPO).
contribution: AgentFlow with 7B backbone achieves average accuracy gains of 14.9% on search, 14.0% on agentic, 14.5% on mathematical tasks, surpassing GPT-4o on some benchmarks.

problem: Program verification remains bottlenecked by hard verification conditions that existing automated theorem provers cannot prove, requiring extensive manual proofs.
approach: NTP4VC introduces the first real-world multi-lingual benchmark for automated VC proving across Isabelle, Lean, and Rocq formal languages from real-world projects like Linux and Contiki-OS.
contribution: The benchmark evaluates LLMs on VC proving and reveals significant challenges remaining for practical program verification.

problem: Open-source search agents rely on commercial LLMs for data or tools, limiting accessibility and scalability for long-horizon information-seeking tasks.
approach: ASearcher trains a single QwQ-32B model via RL using a two-staged process to synthesize training data and large-scale long-horizon RL with up to 128 actions per rollout.
contribution: ASearcher achieves GAIA 58.1, xBench 51.1, and Frames 74.5 using only basic search tools, with further improvements to 71.8, 75.0, and 83.4 using zero-shot enhancements.

problem: LLMs applied to text-rich graph machine learning tasks lack principled understanding of their capabilities, particularly in node classification on heterophilic graphs.
approach: A large-scale controlled evaluation compares LLM-graph interaction modes (prompting, tool-use, code generation) across diverse datasets and graph properties.
contribution: Code generation mode achieves strongest overall performance with especially large gains on long-text or high-degree graphs, and flexibly shifts reliance to most informative input types.

problem: Application of multimodal LLM embeddings to dynamic modalities like audio and video remains underexplored, lacking unified representation spaces.
approach: WAVE employs hierarchical feature fusion and joint multi-modal, multi-task training to create a unified representation space for text, audio, and video with prompt-aware embeddings.
contribution: WAVE sets state-of-the-art on MMEB-v2 video benchmark and achieves superior results in audio and video-to-audio retrieval tasks.

problem: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer models fail to generalize beyond training context windows, collapsing on long-context tasks due to uncontrolled state growth.
approach: Universal Position Interpolation (UPI) unifies Mamba's cumulative decay with Transformer rotary frequency scaling in a training-free method to control state growth.
contribution: UPI extends models from 4K to 64K tokens on PG-19, LongBench and RULER benchmarks without sacrificing short-context accuracy.

problem: Traditional brain modeling methods ignore biological spike characteristics and struggle to reveal dynamic dependencies and causal interactions between brain regions.
approach: Spike-DB encodes fMRI signals as spike trains and learns temporal driving relationships between regions using spike computing paradigm.
contribution: Spike-DB outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy and downstream tasks on epilepsy and Alzheimer's Disease datasets.

problem: The role of brain alignment in LLMs for linguistic competence remains uncertain, despite potential for enhanced safety and trustworthiness.
approach: Brain-misaligned LLMs are intentionally trained to predict brain activity poorly while maintaining high language modeling performance, enabling isolation of brain alignment effects.
contribution: Brain misalignment substantially impairs downstream performance across over 200 linguistic tasks, highlighting the critical role of brain alignment.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning methods struggle to achieve near-optimal performance while leveraging offline trajectories and providing performance guarantees.
approach: Conservative Peng's Q(λ) (CPQL) adapts the Peng's Q(λ) operator for conservative value estimation, achieving implicit behavior regularization through multi-step operators.
contribution: CPQL consistently and significantly outperforms existing offline single-step baselines on D4RL benchmark.

problem: Randomized controlled trials rely on hand-crafted hypotheses and expensive analysis, preventing discovery of effects at scale.
approach: Neural Effect Search turns unstructured trial data into representations via foundation models and interprets them via Sparse Auto Encoder using a recursive stratification procedure.
contribution: The method achieves the first successful unsupervised causal effect identification on real-world scientific trials.

problem: Developing biologically plausible learning algorithms comparable to error backpropagation while using spikes for error propagation remains unresolved.
approach: Bidirectional Spike-based Distillation (BSD) jointly trains feedforward and backward spiking networks to implement perception and memory recall as transformations between spike representations.
contribution: BSD achieves performance comparable to error backpropagation across image recognition, generation, and sequential regression on diverse benchmarks.

problem: LoRA enforces uniform rank across layers despite substantial variation in layer importance, and existing adaptive-rank methods rely on unstable instantaneous gradients.
approach: IGU-LoRA computes within-layer Integrated Gradients sensitivities and applies uncertainty-aware schemes using exponential moving averages for rank allocation.
contribution: IGU-LoRA consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines at matched parameter budgets, improving downstream accuracy and robustness.

problem: Multi-step reasoning tasks are vulnerable to cascading failures where a single incorrect step leads to complete solution breakdown, yet routing treats all steps equally.
approach: TRIM routes only critical steps to larger models using process reward models to identify erroneous steps, with four routing strategies from thresholding to POMDP-based approaches.
contribution: TRIM achieves 6.51x higher cost efficiency on MATH-500 with thresholding, while RL and POMDP policies match expensive models using 80% fewer tokens.

problem: Standard cameras capture limited dynamic range leading to saturated highlights or underexposed shadows, and conventional HDR methods fail to model geometry and motion consistently in 3D.
approach: HDR-NSFF reconstructs dynamic HDR radiance fields from alternatively exposed monocular videos by explicitly modeling 3D scene flow, HDR radiance, and tone mapping end-to-end.
contribution: HDR-NSFF achieves state-of-the-art performance in novel view and time synthesis, recovering fine radiance details and coherent dynamics under challenging exposure variations.

problem: RLHF-based alignment methods can violate Pareto optimality, where a response may be less helpful and more toxic than another yet receive higher reward.
approach: A linear social choice model is analyzed to show polynomial reward models cannot resolve axiom violations, but balanced dataset coverage via design enables loss-based rules to recover guarantees.
contribution: The work provides a recipe for constitutional-style alignment with provable guarantees by enforcing balanced coverage in dataset design.

problem: Traditional MoE models lack explicit constraints ensuring the router's decisions align with experts' capabilities, limiting model performance.
approach: Expert-Router Coupling (ERC) loss couples expert capabilities with router decisions by creating proxy tokens and enforcing mutual activation preferences.
contribution: Pre-training multiple 3B MoE-LLMs with ERC loss demonstrates consistent effectiveness in expert specialization and performance improvements.

problem: LLMs' ability to perform geometric spatial reasoning expressed in procedural code remains underexplored and not systematically evaluated.
approach: GeoGramBench formalizes the Program-to-Geometry task with 500 problems organized by a three-level taxonomy considering geometric complexity rather than mathematical reasoning difficulty.
contribution: Evaluation of 17 frontier LLMs reveals consistent deficiencies, with even the most advanced models achieving less than 50% accuracy at the highest abstraction level.

problem: Graph Neural Networks remain vulnerable to graph-level imbalance encompassing both class imbalance and topological imbalance in graph classification.
approach: UniImb captures multi-scale topological features via learnable personalized perturbations and employs dynamic balanced prototypes with prototype load-balancing optimization.
contribution: UniImb achieves dominant performance across various imbalanced scenarios on 19 datasets including a new large-scale AirGraph dataset.

problem: Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning stems from difficulty reactivating old memories, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning still fails in fully reawakening prior task knowledge.
approach: HippoTune implements a hippocampal EC-DG-CA3-CA1 circuit-inspired iterative retrieval strategy with a latent-space query-retrieve-feedback loop within each Transformer layer.
contribution: HippoTune outperforms classical buffer-free PEFT-CL methods by 5–8% in accuracy across vision benchmarks while reducing training FLOPs by 50%.

problem: Open-ended deep research suffers from static pipelines decoupling planning from evidence acquisition and monolithic generation causing hallucinations and low citation accuracy.
approach: WebWeaver uses a dual-agent framework with a planner iteratively interleaving evidence acquisition with outline optimization and a writer performing hierarchical retrieval and section-by-section writing.
contribution: WebWeaver establishes state-of-the-art performance across DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym benchmarks.

problem: Time series causal discovery methods lack robust performance assessment against assumption violations and practical adoption is hindered by unverifiable strong assumptions.
approach: TCD-Arena provides a modularized testing kit assessing robustness of CD algorithms against stepwise more severe assumption violations via over 50 million individual CD attempts.
contribution: The extensive empirical study reveals nuanced robustness profiles for 27 distinct assumption violations and shows CD ensembles can boost general robustness.

problem: Existing web agent benchmarks measure only task completion while ignoring whether agents complete tasks safely and trustworthily for enterprise adoption.
approach: ST-WebAgentBench provides 222 tasks paired with safety/trustworthiness (ST) policies scored along six dimensions, proposing Completion Under Policy (CuP) metric and Risk Ratio.
contribution: Evaluation shows state-of-the-art agents have average CuP less than two-thirds of nominal completion rate, revealing substantial safety gaps.

problem: Current RAG pipelines use static chunking and flat retrieval, making quality highly sensitive to chunk size while introducing noise and scaling poorly to large corpora.
approach: SmartChunk uses a planner predicting optimal chunk abstraction level and a lightweight compression module producing high-level embeddings via reinforcement learning scheme STITCH.
contribution: SmartChunk outperforms state-of-the-art RAG baselines across five QA benchmarks while reducing cost and demonstrating strong scalability with larger corpora.

problem: Text-guided color editing requires fine-grained manipulation of color attributes while preserving physical consistency, and existing training-free approaches struggle with precise control and consistency.
approach: ColorCtrl leverages attention mechanisms of Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformers by disentangling structure and color through targeted manipulation of attention maps and value tokens.
contribution: ColorCtrl outperforms existing training-free approaches and achieves state-of-the-art performance on SD3 and FLUX.1-dev, surpassing FLUX.1 Kontext Max and GPT-4o in consistency.

problem: Guidance with first-order Taylor approximation for discrete data is inappropriate because approximation error is large in discrete state spaces.
approach: A novel guidance framework for discrete data derives exact transition rates for desired distributions given learned discrete flow matching models, requiring only one forward pass per step.
contribution: The unified framework encompasses existing guidance methods and effectively applies to masked diffusion models for energy-guided and preference-aligned generation.

problem: Nearest neighbor search in high-dimensional settings with noisy low-dimensional subspace data requires understanding when denoising enables accurate recovery.
approach: Theoretical analysis proves SVD denoises data for noise level σ in O(1/k^1/4) and establishes matching lower bounds showing necessity of this threshold.
contribution: SVD identifies correct neighbors in uncorrupted data even when noise makes NNs in noisy data different from uncorrupted data, a regime not captured in prior work.

problem: LLM-based planning agents in Minecraft begin with flawed priors and fail to correct them through prompting even with feedback.
approach: XENON algorithmically revises knowledge from experience via Adaptive Dependency Graph and Failure-aware Action Memory using past successes and failures.
contribution: XENON surpasses prior agents in knowledge learning and long-horizon planning on multiple Minecraft benchmarks, even with 7B LLM.

problem: How RL and SFT shape reasoning capabilities in LLMs remains largely elusive despite their widespread use for improving reasoning.
approach: A novel analysis framework quantifies reasoning paths at trajectory-level and step-level using reasoning graphs to capture qualitative changes under each training process.
contribution: RL compresses incorrect trajectories while SFT expands correct ones; RL steepens decay rates of node metrics by 2.5x while SFT reduces them to one-third.

problem: Point tracking in long videos suffers from feature drifting because target tracking points undergo increasing variation over time and RNN-like temporal modeling is insufficient.
approach: TAPTRv3 uses Context-aware Cross-Attention for spatial feature querying and Visibility-aware Long-Temporal Attention for temporal attention over all past frames.
contribution: TAPTRv3 surpasses TAPTRv2 by large margins on challenging datasets and achieves state-of-the-art performance even compared to methods trained on large-scale internal data.

problem: Extending amortized Bayesian inference to hierarchical models with massive datasets and thousands of parameters remains challenging due to stability issues.
approach: The method couples adaptive solvers with error-damping compositional estimator based on compositional score matching for robust hierarchical Bayesian updating.
contribution: The approach remains stable with hundreds of thousands of data points and parameters, validated on toy examples, autoregressive models, and real microscopy applications.

problem: Progress in neural code intelligence for visual-programmatic interfaces is impeded by scarcity of high-quality multimodal code data.
approach: JanusCoder introduces a synthesis toolkit leveraging reciprocal synergies between modalities to create JanusCode-800K corpus, training unified visual-programmatic code generation models.
contribution: JanusCoder with 7B-14B models approaches or exceeds commercial models on text-centric and vision-centric coding tasks.

problem: Per-frame optimization in Gaussian splatting for dynamic scenes causes overfitting to instantaneous states rather than learning true motion dynamics.
approach: Mango-GS uses a temporal Transformer to learn complex motion dependencies across frame windows with decoupled position and latent codes in sparse control nodes.
contribution: Mango-GS achieves state-of-the-art quality and fast rendering speed for high-fidelity reconstruction and real-time rendering of dynamic scenes.
